sanskrit: jahi krodham imaṃ sādho na krudhyanti bhavadvidhāḥ parasya patnī sā devī prasīdasva sureśvara
english: Abandon this anger, O virtuous one — those of your stature do not grow wrathful. She is the wife of another, that divine lady. Be appeased, O lord of the gods.

sanskrit: nivartaya manaḥ pāpāt paradārābhimarśanāt devarājo 'si bhadraṃ te prajā dharmeṇa pālaya
english: Turn your mind away from sin, from the violation of another man's wife. You are the king of the gods — may it be well with you. Rule your subjects by righteousness.

sanskrit: evam ukto na jagrāha tad vacaḥ kāmamohitaḥ atha devān uvācedam indraṃ prati surādhipaḥ
english: Addressed thus, he did not heed those words, for he was deluded by desire. Then the lord of the gods spoke thus to the gods, with regard to Indra:

sanskrit: ahalyā dharṣitā pūrvam ṛṣipatnī yaśasvinī jīvato bhartur indreṇa sa vaḥ kiṃ na nivāritaḥ
english: Ahalyā, the illustrious wife of a sage, was violated of old by Indra while her husband still lived — why did you not restrain him then?

sanskrit: bahūni ca nṛśaṃsāni kṛtānīndreṇa vai purā vaidharmyāṇy upadhāś caiva sa vaḥ kiṃ na nivāritaḥ
english: Many cruel and unrighteous deeds, many deceits, were committed by Indra in former times — why did you not restrain him then?

sanskrit: upatiṣṭhatu māṃ devī etad asyā hitaṃ param yuṣmākaṃ ca sadā devāḥ śivam evaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Let the goddess come to attend upon me — this is the highest good for her. And for you, O gods, there shall always be welfare if it is so.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ indrāṇīm ānayiṣyāmo yathecchasi divaspate jahi krodham imaṃ vīra prīto bhava sureśvara
english: The gods said: We shall bring Indrāṇī to you as you desire, O lord of heaven. Abandon this anger, O hero. Be pleased, O lord of the gods.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca ity uktvā te tadā devā ṛṣibhiḥ saha bhārata jagmur bṛhaspatiṃ vaktum indrāṇīṃ cāśubhaṃ vacaḥ
english: Śalya said: Having spoken thus, the gods, together with the seers, O Bhārata, went to Bṛhaspati to speak to Indrāṇī those inauspicious words.

sanskrit: jānīmaḥ śaraṇaṃ prāptam indrāṇīṃ tava veśmani dattābhayāṃ ca viprendra tvayā devarṣisattama
english: We know that Indrāṇī has come to you for refuge, into your home, and that you have granted her freedom from fear, O best of the twice-born, O foremost of divine seers.

sanskrit: te tvāṃ devāḥ sagandharvā ṛṣayaś ca mahādyute prasādayanti cendrāṇī nahuṣāya pradīyatām
english: The gods, together with the gandharvas and the seers, O greatly resplendent one, entreat you — let Indrāṇī be given over to Nahuṣa.

sanskrit: indrād viśiṣṭo nahuṣo devarājo mahādyutiḥ vṛṇotv iyaṃ varārohā bhartṛtve varavarṇinī
english: Nahuṣa surpasses Indra and is the great-resplendent king of the gods — let this woman of beautiful hips and fair complexion choose him as her husband.

sanskrit: evam ukte tu sā devī bāṣpam utsṛjya sasvaram uvāca rudatī dīnā bṛhaspatim idaṃ vacaḥ
english: When this was said, that divine lady, weeping with a cry, shed her tears and spoke these piteous words to Bṛhaspati:

sanskrit: nāham icchāmi nahuṣaṃ patim anvāsya taṃ prabhum śaraṇāgatāsmi te brahmaṃs trāhi māṃ mahato bhayāt
english: I do not desire Nahuṣa as my husband — I will wait upon that lord, my husband. I have come to you for refuge, O Brahman; save me from this great fear.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca śaraṇāgatāṃ na tyajeyam indrāṇi mama niścitam dharmajñāṃ dharmaśīlāṃ ca na tyaje tvām anindite
english: Bṛhaspati said: I would never abandon one who has sought refuge — this is my firm resolve, O Indrāṇī. You who know dharma and are devoted to dharma — I shall not forsake you, O blameless one.

sanskrit: nākāryaṃ kartum icchāmi brāhmaṇaḥ san viśeṣataḥ śrutadharmā satyaśīlo jānan dharmānuśāsanam
english: I have no wish to do what ought not be done, especially being a brahmin who is learned in dharma, who is devoted to truth, and who knows the teaching of righteousness.

sanskrit: nāham etat kariṣyāmi gacchadhvaṃ vai surottamāḥ asmiṃś cārthe purā gītaṃ brahmaṇā śrūyatām idam
english: I shall not do this. Depart, O best of gods. And in this matter, hear what was sung of old by Brahmā:

sanskrit: na tasya bījaṃ rohati bījakāle; na cāsya varṣaṃ varṣati varṣakāle bhītaṃ prapannaṃ pradadāti śatrave; na so 'ntaraṃ labhate trāṇam icchan
english: His seed does not sprout at the time of sowing; the rain does not fall for him at the time of rain — one who surrenders a frightened refugee to the enemy finds no refuge himself when he desires protection.

sanskrit: mogham annaṃ vindati cāpy acetāḥ; svargāl lokād bhraśyati naṣṭaceṣṭaḥ bhītaṃ prapannaṃ pradadāti yo vai; na tasya havyaṃ pratigṛhṇanti devāḥ
english: He obtains his food in vain, devoid of wisdom; he falls from the heavenly realm, his efforts lost — one who surrenders a frightened refugee: the gods do not accept his oblations.

sanskrit: pramīyate cāsya prajā hy akāle; sadā vivāsaṃ pitaro 'sya kurvate bhītaṃ prapannaṃ pradadāti śatrave; sendrā devāḥ praharanty asya vajram
english: His offspring perish untimely; his ancestors always make him homeless — one who surrenders a frightened refugee: the gods together with Indra hurl the thunderbolt upon him.

sanskrit: etad evaṃ vijānan vai na dāsyāmi śacīm imām indrāṇīṃ viśrutāṃ loke śakrasya mahiṣīṃ priyām
english: Knowing this to be so, I shall not give away this Śacī, this Indrāṇī renowned in the world, the beloved queen of Śakra.

sanskrit: asyā hitaṃ bhaved yac ca mama cāpi hitaṃ bhavet kriyatāṃ tat suraśreṣṭhā na hi dāsyāmy ahaṃ śacīm
english: Whatever would be for her welfare and whatever would be for my welfare — let that be done, O best of gods. I shall not give up Śacī.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca atha devās tam evāhur gurum aṅgirasāṃ varam kathaṃ sunītaṃ tu bhaven mantrayasva bṛhaspate
english: Śalya said: Then the gods spoke to him, the foremost among the sages of the Aṅgiras line: "How then may right policy be achieved? Deliberate upon it, O Bṛhaspati."

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca nahuṣaṃ yācatāṃ devī kiṃ cit kālāntaraṃ śubhā indrāṇīhitam etad dhi tathāsmākaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Bṛhaspati said: Let the auspicious lady request of Nahuṣa a little interval of time — this is indeed for the good of Indrāṇī, and likewise it shall be for our good as well.

sanskrit: bahuvighnakaraḥ kālaḥ kālaḥ kālaṃ nayiṣyati darpito balavāṃś cāpi nahuṣo varasaṃśrayāt
english: Time is the creator of many obstacles; time will lead time onward. Nahuṣa, though arrogant and powerful by reason of the boon he received, will be brought down by time.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca tatas tena tathokte tu prītā devās tam abruvan brahman sādhv idam uktaṃ te hitaṃ sarvadivaukasām evam etad dvijaśreṣṭha devī ceyaṃ prasādyatām
english: Śalya said: When he had spoken thus, the pleased gods addressed him: "O Brahman, what you have said is excellent and for the welfare of all the dwellers in heaven. O best of the twice-born, it is just so — and let this goddess too be persuaded."

sanskrit: tataḥ samastā indrāṇīṃ devāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ ūcur vacanam avyagrā lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: Then all the gods, with Fire at their head, spoke to Indrāṇī calmly, desiring the welfare of the worlds:

sanskrit: tvayā jagad idaṃ sarvaṃ dhṛtaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam ekapatny asi satyā ca gacchasva nahuṣaṃ prati
english: By you this entire world, both the moving and the unmoving, is upheld. You are faithful to one husband and truthful — go now towards Nahuṣa.

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ tvām abhikāmaś ca vinaśiṣyati pārthivaḥ nahuṣo devi śakraś ca suraiśvaryam avāpsyati
english: Nahuṣa, who lusts for you, O goddess, will swiftly be destroyed, and Śakra shall regain his sovereignty over the gods.

sanskrit: evaṃ viniścayaṃ kṛtvā indrāṇī kāryasiddhaye abhyagacchata savrīḍā nahuṣaṃ ghoradarśanam
english: Having thus resolved upon this plan for the accomplishment of the purpose, Indrāṇī, overcome with shame, went toward Nahuṣa of terrible aspect.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tāṃ nahuṣaś cāpi vayorūpasamanvitām samahṛṣyata duṣṭātmā kāmopahatacetanaḥ
english: Seeing her, endowed with youth and beauty, Nahuṣa of wicked soul, his mind overwhelmed by desire, was greatly thrilled.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca atha tām abravīd dṛṣṭvā nahuṣo devarāṭ tadā trayāṇām api lokānām aham indraḥ śucismite bhajasva māṃ varārohe patitve varavarṇini
english: Śalya said: Then, looking at her, Nahuṣa the king of gods spoke to her: "I am Indra of all three worlds, O bright-smiling one. Accept me, O lady of beautiful hips and fair complexion, as your husband."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu sā devī nahuṣeṇa pativratā prāvepata bhayodvignā pravāte kadalī yathā
english: Addressed thus by Nahuṣa, the devoted wife, agitated with fear, trembled like a plantain tree in the wind.

sanskrit: namasya sā tu brahmāṇaṃ kṛtvā śirasi cāñjalim devarājam athovāca nahuṣaṃ ghoradarśanam
english: Reverencing Brahmā with joined palms raised to her head, she then spoke to Nahuṣa, that king of gods of terrible aspect:

sanskrit: kālam icchāmy ahaṃ labdhuṃ kiṃ cit tvattaḥ sureśvara na hi vijñāyate śakraḥ prāptaḥ kiṃ vā kva vā gataḥ
english: "I desire to obtain a little time from you, O lord of the gods. For it is not known whether Śakra has met some end, or where he has gone."

sanskrit: tattvam etat tu vijñāya yadi na jñāyate prabho tato 'haṃ tvām upasthāsye satyam etad bravīmi te evam uktaḥ sa indrāṇyā nahuṣaḥ prītimān abhūt
english: "Having ascertained this truth, if he is indeed not to be found, O lord, then I shall attend upon you — this I tell you truly." Addressed thus by Indrāṇī, Nahuṣa became pleased.

sanskrit: nahuṣa uvāca evaṃ bhavatu suśroṇi yathā mām abhibhāṣase jñātvā cāgamanaṃ kāryaṃ satyam etad anusmareḥ
english: Nahuṣa said: So be it, O lady of beautiful hips, as you have spoken to me. And having ascertained the matter, remember that your coming to me is an obligation of truth.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca nahuṣeṇa visṛṣṭā ca niścakrāma tataḥ śubhā bṛhaspatiniketaṃ sā jagāma ca tapasvinī
english: Śalya said: Dismissed by Nahuṣa, that auspicious and ascetic woman departed and went to the dwelling of Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ saṃśrutya ca vaco devāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ mantrayām āsur ekāgrāḥ śakrārthaṃ rājasattama
english: Hearing her words, the gods with Fire at their head deliberated with single-minded purpose for the sake of Śakra, O best of kings.

sanskrit: devadevena saṃgamya viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā ūcuś cainaṃ samudvignā vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradāḥ
english: Meeting with Viṣṇu, the god of gods, the all-pervading one, those skilled in speech spoke to him in great distress:

sanskrit: brahmahatyābhibhūto vai śakraḥ suragaṇeśvaraḥ gatiś ca nas tvaṃ deveśa pūrvajo jagataḥ prabhuḥ rakṣārthaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viṣṇutvam upajagmivān
english: "Śakra, the lord of the host of gods, is indeed overwhelmed by the sin of brahmin-slaughter. You are our refuge, O lord of gods, the firstborn, the master of the universe, who has assumed the state of Viṣṇu for the protection of all beings."

sanskrit: tvadvīryān nihate vṛtre vāsavo brahmahatyayā vṛtaḥ suragaṇaśreṣṭha mokṣaṃ tasya vinirdiśa
english: "By your valor Vṛtra was slain, and Vāsava is now beset by the guilt of brahmin-slaughter. O foremost among the hosts of gods, prescribe his liberation."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā devānāṃ viṣṇur abravīt mām eva yajatāṃ śakraḥ pāvayiṣyāmi vajriṇam
english: Hearing those words of the gods, Viṣṇu said: "Let Śakra worship me alone — I shall purify the wielder of the thunderbolt."

sanskrit: puṇyena hayamedhena mām iṣṭvā pākaśāsanaḥ punar eṣyati devānām indratvam akutobhayaḥ
english: "Having worshipped me with the meritorious horse-sacrifice, the chastiser of Pāka shall once again attain the lordship over the gods, free from all fear."

sanskrit: svakarmabhiś ca nahuṣo nāśaṃ yāsyati durmatiḥ kaṃ cit kālam imaṃ devā marṣayadhvam atandritāḥ
english: "And Nahuṣa of wicked mind shall come to ruin through his own deeds. Bear with this state for a little while, O gods — remain vigilant without delay."

sanskrit: śrutvā viṣṇoḥ śubhāṃ satyāṃ tāṃ vāṇīm amṛtopamām tataḥ sarve suragaṇāḥ sopādhyāyāḥ saharṣibhiḥ yatra śakro bhayodvignas taṃ deśam upacakramuḥ
english: Hearing that auspicious, true, and nectar-like speech of Viṣṇu, all the hosts of gods, together with their teachers and with the seers, approached the place where Śakra, afflicted with fear, was hiding.

sanskrit: tatrāśvamedhaḥ sumahān mahendrasya mahātmanaḥ vavṛte pāvanārthaṃ vai brahmahatyāpaho nṛpa
english: There a most grand horse-sacrifice of the great-souled Mahendra was performed for the purpose of purification — the destroyer of the sin of brahmin-slaughter, O king.

sanskrit: vibhajya brahmahatyāṃ tu vṛkṣeṣu ca nadīṣu ca parvateṣu pṛthivyāṃ ca strīṣu caiva yudhiṣṭhira
english: Distributing the guilt of brahmin-slaughter among trees, rivers, mountains, the earth, and women, O Yudhiṣṭhira —

sanskrit: saṃvibhajya ca bhūteṣu visṛjya ca sureśvaraḥ vijvaraḥ pūtapāpmā ca vāsavo 'bhavad ātmavān
english: — distributing it among all beings and releasing it, the lord of the gods became free of fever, purified of sin; Vāsava became himself again.

sanskrit: akampyaṃ nahuṣaṃ sthānād dṛṣṭvā ca balasūdanaḥ tejoghnaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ varadānāc ca duḥsaham
english: Seeing Nahuṣa, immovable in his position and by reason of the boon he had received, the slayer of Bala beheld him as one who diminishes the splendor of all beings and who is difficult to overcome.

sanskrit: tataḥ śacīpatir vīraḥ punar eva vyanaśyata adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ kālākāṅkṣī cacāra ha
english: Then the heroic lord of Śacī vanished once more, became invisible to all beings, and wandered about awaiting the right time.

sanskrit: pranaṣṭe tu tataḥ śakre śacī śokasamanvitā hā śakreti tadā devī vilalāpa suduḥkhitā
english: When Śakra had thus disappeared, Śacī, filled with grief, lamented in great distress, crying out: "Ah, Śakra!"

sanskrit: yadi dattaṃ yadi hutaṃ guravas toṣitā yadi ekabhartṛtvam evāstu satyaṃ yady asti vā mayi
english: "If I have given gifts, if I have offered oblations, if I have pleased my elders, if it is true that I have been faithful to one husband alone, if there is any truth in me —

sanskrit: puṇyāṃ cemām ahaṃ divyāṃ pravṛttām uttarāyaṇe devīṃ rātriṃ namasyāmi sidhyatāṃ me manorathaḥ
english: — I shall worship this sacred, divine Night-goddess who moves during the northward course of the sun. May my heart's desire be fulfilled."

sanskrit: prayatā ca niśāṃ devīm upātiṣṭhata tatra sā pativratātvāt satyena sopaśrutim athākarot
english: With ritual purity she worshipped the Night-goddess there, and through the power of her vow of devotion to her husband and through truth, she summoned the goddess Upaśruti.

sanskrit: yatrāste devarājo 'sau taṃ deśaṃ darśayasva me ity āhopaśrutiṃ devī satyaṃ satyena dṛśyatām
english: "Show me the place where that king of gods abides" — thus the goddess called upon Upaśruti: "Let truth be revealed through truth."

sanskrit: śalya uvāca athaināṃ rupiṇīṃ sādhvīm upātiṣṭhad upaśrutiḥ tāṃ vayorūpasaṃpannāṃ dṛṣṭvā devīm upasthitām
english: Śalya said: Then Upaśruti, taking a beautiful form, appeared before that virtuous lady. Seeing the goddess arrived, endowed with youth and beauty —

sanskrit: indrāṇī saṃprahṛṣṭā sā saṃpūjyainām apṛcchata icchāmi tvām ahaṃ jñātuṃ kā tvaṃ brūhi varānane
english: — Indrāṇī, greatly delighted, honored her and then asked: "I wish to know who you are. Tell me, O fair-faced one."

sanskrit: upaśrutir uvāca upaśrutir ahaṃ devi tavāntikam upāgatā darśanaṃ caiva saṃprāptā tava satyena toṣitā
english: Upaśruti said: I am Upaśruti, O goddess, come to your presence. I have obtained the vision of you and am gratified by your truthfulness.

sanskrit: pativratāsi yuktā ca yamena niyamena ca darśayiṣyāmi te śakraṃ devaṃ vṛtraniṣūdanam kṣipram anvehi bhadraṃ te drakṣyase surasattamam
english: "You are devoted to your husband and disciplined in restraint and vows. I shall show you Śakra, the god who slew Vṛtra. Follow quickly — may it be well with you; you shall see the foremost of the gods."

sanskrit: śalya uvāca tatas tāṃ prasthitāṃ devīm indrāṇī sā samanvagāt devāraṇyāny atikramya parvatāṃś ca bahūṃs tataḥ himavantam atikramya uttaraṃ pārśvam āgamat
english: Śalya said: Then Indrāṇī followed behind that goddess as she set forth, crossing the divine forests and many mountains; crossing the Himavān, she reached the northern slopes.

sanskrit: samudraṃ ca samāsādya bahuyojanavistṛtam āsasāda mahādvīpaṃ nānādrumalatāvṛtam
english: Reaching the ocean, extending for many leagues, she came to a great island covered with diverse trees and creeping plants.

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyat saro divyaṃ nānāśakunibhir vṛtam śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ tāvad evāyataṃ śubham
english: There she beheld a divine lake, surrounded by many kinds of birds, a hundred leagues wide and equally long — beautiful.

sanskrit: tatra divyāni padmāni pañcavarṇāni bhārata ṣaṭpadair upagītāni praphullāni sahasraśaḥ
english: There, O Bhārata, thousands of divine lotuses of five colors bloomed in full blossom, humming with bees that sang around them.

sanskrit: padmasya bhittvā nālaṃ ca viveśa sahitā tayā bisatantupraviṣṭaṃ ca tatrāpaśyac chatakratum
english: Piercing the stalk of a lotus, she entered together with her guide; and there, hidden within the filament of the lotus, she beheld the hundred-sacrificed Śatakratu.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā ca susūkṣmeṇa rūpeṇāvasthitaṃ prabhum sūkṣmarūpadharā devī babhūvopaśrutiś ca sā
english: Seeing the lord dwelling there in a most minute form, the goddess too assumed a minute form, as did Upaśruti.

sanskrit: indraṃ tuṣṭāva cendrāṇī viśrutaiḥ pūrvakarmabhiḥ stūyamānas tato devaḥ śacīm āha puraṃdaraḥ
english: Indrāṇī praised Indra with accounts of his renowned former deeds. Being thus praised, the god Puraṃdara then spoke to Śacī:

sanskrit: kimartham asi saṃprāptā vijñātaś ca kathaṃ tv aham tataḥ sā kathayām āsa nahuṣasya viceṣṭitam
english: "For what purpose have you come here, and how did you find me?" Then she proceeded to tell him all the deeds of Nahuṣa:

sanskrit: indratvaṃ triṣu lokeṣu prāpya vīryamadānvitaḥ darpāviṣṭaś ca duṣṭātmā mām uvāca śatakrato upatiṣṭha mām iti krūraḥ kālaṃ ca kṛtavān mama
english: "Having obtained the lordship over the three worlds, filled with the intoxication of valor, that wicked-souled one, seized by arrogance, spoke to me, O Śatakratu: 'Attend upon me,' the cruel one said, and he set a time-limit upon me."

sanskrit: yadi na trāsyasi vibho kariṣyati sa māṃ vaśe etena cāhaṃ saṃtaptā prāptā śakra tavāntikam jahi raudraṃ mahābāho nahuṣaṃ pāpaniścayam
english: "If you do not rescue me, O mighty one, he will bring me under his power. Tormented by this, I have come to you, O Śakra. Slay Nahuṣa, that fierce, long-armed one whose resolve is evil."

sanskrit: prakāśayasva cātmānaṃ daityadānavasūdana tejaḥ samāpnuhi vibho devarājyaṃ praśādhi ca
english: "Reveal yourself, O slayer of the daityas and dānavas. Regain your splendor, O mighty one. Rule over the kingdom of the gods once more."

sanskrit: śalya uvāca evam uktaḥ sa bhagavāñ śacyā punar athābravīt vikramasya na kālo 'yaṃ nahuṣo balavattaraḥ
english: Śalya said: Addressed thus by Śacī, that blessed one replied again: "This is not the time for valor — Nahuṣa is the more powerful."

sanskrit: vivardhitaś ca ṛṣibhir havyaiḥ kavyaiś ca bhāmini nītim atra vidhāsyāmi devi tāṃ kartum arhasi
english: "And he has been strengthened by the seers through oblations to the gods and to the ancestors, O passionate one. Here I shall devise a strategy, O goddess — you must carry it out."

sanskrit: guhyaṃ caitat tvayā kāryaṃ nākhyātavyaṃ śubhe kva cit gatvā nahuṣam ekānte bravīhi tanumadhyame
english: "This must be kept secret by you and disclosed nowhere, O auspicious one. Go and speak to Nahuṣa in private, O slender-waisted one."

sanskrit: ṛṣiyānena divyena mām upaihi jagatpate evaṃ tava vaśe prītā bhaviṣyāmīti taṃ vada
english: "Tell him: 'Come to me drawn by a divine vehicle borne by seers, O lord of the universe — then, pleased, I shall come under your power.'"

sanskrit: ity uktā devarājena patnī sā kamalekṣaṇā evam astv ity athoktvā tu jagāma nahuṣaṃ prati
english: Addressed thus by the king of gods, that wife of lotus eyes said, "So be it," and went toward Nahuṣa.

sanskrit: nahuṣas tāṃ tato dṛṣṭvā vismito vākyam abravīt svāgataṃ te varārohe kiṃ karomi śucismite
english: Nahuṣa then, seeing her, spoke in surprise: "Welcome to you, O lady of beautiful hips. What may I do for you, O bright-smiling one?"

sanskrit: bhaktaṃ māṃ bhaja kalyāṇi kim icchasi manasvini tava kalyāṇi yat kāryaṃ tat kariṣye sumadhyame
english: "Accept me who am devoted to you, O auspicious lady. What do you desire, O wise one? Whatever needs to be done for you, O fair-waisted one, I shall do it."

sanskrit: na ca vrīḍā tvayā kāryā suśroṇi mayi viśvasa satyena vai śape devi kartāsmi vacanaṃ tava
english: "And you need have no shame before me, O beautiful-hipped one. Trust me. I swear by truth, O goddess, I shall do your bidding."

sanskrit: indrāṇy uvāca yo me tvayā kṛtaḥ kālas tam ākāṅkṣe jagatpate tatas tvam eva bhartā me bhaviṣyasi surādhipa
english: Indrāṇī said: I am awaiting the time you have set for me, O lord of the universe. After that, you shall indeed be my husband, O lord of the gods.

sanskrit: kāryaṃ ca hṛdi me yat tad devarājāvadhāraya vakṣyāmi yadi me rājan priyam etat kariṣyasi vākyaṃ praṇayasaṃyuktaṃ tataḥ syāṃ vaśagā tava
english: "And the desire I hold in my heart — hear it, O king of gods. I shall tell it to you: if you, O king, will do what is dear to me, this word spoken with affection — then I shall become subject to your will."
